Heard Sri.B.S.Karthikeyan, who appears through video conference and represents the appellant.

2. This appeal is the outcome of the award that is passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Nanjangud, in MVC No.1278/2017 dated 08.01.2021.
3.
Though notice was served upon the respondent, respondent has not chosen to contest the matter.
4. On the ground that she sustained grievous injury in a road traffic accident and became permanently and completely disabled, the respondent filed a petition claiming compensation.

The Tribunal through the impugned order held that the respondent is entitled to a sum of Rs.6,73,715/-
as compensation.
The appellant against whom the liability is fastened is before this Court.
NC: 2026:KHC:253 HC-KAR 5.
Arguing the matter, learned counsel for the appellant states that the compensation granted is exorbitant and excessive.
Learned counsel submits that the appellant is aggrieved only by the percentage of disability assessed by the tribunal.
Learned counsel submits that as per the evidence of PW2, the respondent suffers with disability of 70% in respect of right upper limb.
However, the tribunal took the disability in respect of whole body as 60%.
Learned counsel submits that the tribunal ought to have taken 1/3rd of 70% as whole body disability.
Learned counsel thereby seeks to reduce the sum that is awarded as compensation towards loss of future earnings.
6. It is not in dispute that the respondent was working as house maid as on the date of accident.

Equally it is not in dispute that due to the accident there was traumatic amputation upto upper Divisional Controller vs Smt Santha on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186052187/
2 1/3rd of right upper limb.

sentences.text: A human being of any gender who loses his/her right upper limb will not be in a position to attend any work which can be done with the upper limbs for eking out the livelihood.
Here is a case where the respondent/claimant aged about 63 years working as house maid lost her right upper limb upto 1/3rd.
Therefore, NC: 2026:KHC:253 HC-KAR undoubtedly she will not be in a position either to attend her normal pursuits on her own as before or attend her work as house maid.

Therefore, this Court is of the view that the Tribunal did not err in taking disability in respect of whole body as 60% and ultimately awarding compensation of Rs.3,02,400/- towards loss of future income.
Thus, this Court is of the view that there are no merits in the appeal.
Resultantly, the appeal stands dismissed.

Sd/-
